title: Worktrees
description: Git worktrees are great for agentic coding, because they allow you to work on multiple branches of a repo at the same time, by keeping them in different directories. Each worktree gets its own VS Code window with Mirror VS.
notGitRepo: This workspace is not a Git repository. Open a workspace with a Git repository to set up worktrees.
multiRootNotSupported: Worktrees are not supported in multi-root workspaces. Please open a single folder to use worktrees.
subfolderNotSupported: This workspace is a subfolder of a Git repository. Please open the repository root to use worktrees.
includeFileExists: .worktreeinclude file found. Files will be copied to new worktrees.
noIncludeFileHint: Worktrees are created with just the files from their branch. If you want to copy over local files like .env and node_modules, include them in a .worktreeinclude file at the root of the repository.
deleteWarning: This can't be undone. It will delete:
deleteWarningBranch: The branch and any uncommitted changes
deleteWarningFiles: All files in the worktree directory
deleteNoticeLarge: If this is a large repository, it may take a little while.
createModalDescription: Worktrees keep new changes in an isolated sandbox under .mirror-vs to keep your original code and main worktree safe.

taskIsolation.title: Isolate tasks in temporary Git Worktrees
taskIsolation.enabledDesc: When enabled, an isolated temporary worktree is created only if you explicitly ask for one in your prompt (e.g. 'run in sandbox'). Otherwise, tasks run directly in your active working tree.
taskIsolation.disabledDesc: Tasks execute directly in your active working tree without creating temporary worktrees.
taskIsolation.enabledShort: Only when explicitly requested in prompt
taskIsolation.tooltip: Tasks run directly in your selected worktree by default. When enabled, a temporary sandbox worktree is created only if you explicitly request it in your prompt.

selector.title: Worktrees
selector.description: Git worktrees keep new changes in a sandbox to keep your original code and main worktree safe.
selector.info: Git worktrees allow you to work on multiple branches in separate folders under .mirror-vs. We use this to keep new changes in a sandbox so your original code and main worktree remain completely safe.
